title: Belgian Waffle Platter
subtitle: Crisp yeasted waffles with whipped butter, syrup, and fresh berries.
description: Crisp Belgian waffles stacked on a platter with butter and syrup. Griddle in batches, hold warm, and let the crew build their own plate.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.notes: separated, yolks in batter, whites whipped

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Belgian Waffle Platter in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.instruction: Whisk flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Stir in warm milk, egg yolks, and melted butter until smooth. Let rest 15 minutes so yeast activates and batter thickens slightly.

steps.title: Fold in whipped whites
steps.instruction: Beat egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold one-third into the batter to lighten, then fold in the rest gently so volume stays airy—do not deflate with heavy stirring.

steps.title: Preheat irons
steps.instruction: Heat Belgian waffle irons to medium-high (most units reach roughly 375°F surface temp). Lightly oil plates if your iron requires it. Keep a rack and sheet pan ready in a 200°F oven.

steps.title: Bake the waffles
steps.instruction: Pour batter to cover the grid without overflowing. Close iron and bake 4–5 minutes per waffle until deep golden and crisp at the edges. Transfer to the rack in the warm oven—never stack.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Belgian Waffle Platter onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Platter and serve
steps.instruction: Arrange waffles on a large warm platter with bowls of whipped butter, warmed maple syrup, and berries. Serve immediately and bake remaining batches while the crew eats.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Belgian Waffle Platter — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Run two irons in parallel if available so eight waffles finish within 15 minutes.
Hold waffles on a rack in a 200°F oven—stacking steams away the crisp crust.
Warm syrup in a small pot on low with a ladle at the line for fast self-serve.
cleanupNotes: Wipe waffle iron plates while warm with a damp cloth—never submerge electric units.
Rinse mixing bowls before batter dries and hardens on the whisk.
leftovers: Toast leftover waffles at 350°F for 6 minutes directly on the rack to re-crisp.
Use stale waffles as bread in a Monte Cristo-style sandwich bake with ham and cheese.
